sourceTitle: Three addresses on the relations subsisting between the white and colored people of the United States
description: "Three Addresses on the Relations Subsisting Between the White and Colored People of the United States" by Frederick Douglass is a collection of orations delivered in the late 19th century, specifically in the 1880s. This work discusses the complex and often fraught dynamics between black and white citizens in America, particularly in the wake of emancipation and the ongoing struggles for civil rights and social equality.
